New RBI ATM Rules: How to Keep Banking Fees Low

Stuti TalwarSeptember 1, 2026
1,047 1 minute read
Share
Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Telegram
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:13
Instaread

 ATMs have made  banking a breeze, allowing quick access to cash without long waits at  bank branches. However, using these machines isn’t always as free as it seems—especially since rules and charges change from time to time. Recently, the Reserve Bank of India refreshed its guidelines for ATM transactions, and these updates can impact how much you pay in fees. Staying on top of these changes helps you manage your money more wisely.

Open Savings Account

For those living in metro areas, three free ATM transactions per month are allowed. If your account is based in a non-metro city, you get up to five free ATM actions each month. It’s important to note that these free transactions don’t only cover cash withdrawals—they also include checking your balance and other non-financial activities. Once you cross your free quota, banks apply a charge for every transaction beyond the limit.

Charges and Rules for Extra Transactions

If you exceed your monthly free allowance, be ready for higher charges. Financial transactions like withdrawing cash may cost up to ₹23 each time, including taxes. For other tasks, such as balance inquiries, charges can go as high as ₹11. The actual amount may differ slightly across banks, so it’s wise to check with your own bank for their specific rules.

Bank

There are also new regulations around high-value cash movement. In case your deposits or withdrawals reach ₹20 lakh or more in a financial year, providing your PAN and Aadhaar details is a must. Such transactions are now reported to keep financial systems transparent and discourage unaccounted money.

Locate Nearby ATMs

Practical Tips for Saving on ATM Fees

Nobody likes paying avoidable charges. Here are some smart strategies for managing ATM costs:

  • Opt for your bank’s own ATMs to enjoy the maximum number of free transactions.
  • Handle routine banking—like checking balances or transferring money—through mobile apps or online portals.
  • Monitor your monthly ATM usage so you stay within your free limit.

Adopting these habits means more control over your funds and less spend on banking fees. Careful planning helps you use ATMs efficiently, making sure convenience doesn’t come with extra costs. Keep these tips in mind and make the most of your banking experience, fee-free.
